translationRepairs.before: Retired counselor Dong Zhongshu still advised Zhang Tang on classical jurisprudence, yielding 232 Spring and Autumn case rulings grounded in canonical debate.
translationRepairs.after: When former Chancellor of Jiaodong Dong Zhongshu retired because of age and illness, the court repeatedly sent Commandant of Justice Zhang Tang to his humble lane to consult him on policy questions; Dong Zhongshu then composed the Spring and Autumn Adjudications of 232 cases, answering from the classics in detail.
translationRepairs.reason: The existing proposed wording leaves Zhang Tang as the nearest subject of “he then composed,” but 於是作《春秋折獄》 refers to Dong Zhongshu. Naming Dong Zhongshu again removes the residual attribution error.

translationRepairs.before: Wang Tong again submitted words, saying, "The responsible offices have carelessly judged that what I submitted cannot be put into effect.
translationRepairs.after: Liang Tong again submitted words, saying, "The responsible offices have carelessly judged that what I submitted cannot be put into effect.
translationRepairs.reason: 統 is Liang Tong, the memorialist introduced in s0050. The existing proposal repairs only the parallel idiomatic field.

translationRepairs.before: The emperor ordered the Secretaries to question him about the circumstances. Wang Tong again replied, speaking fully on why government and punishments should be changed.
translationRepairs.after: The emperor ordered the Secretaries to question him about the circumstances. Liang Tong again replied, speaking fully on why government and punishments should be changed.
translationRepairs.reason: 統 is Liang Tong, not Wang Tong. The existing proposal repairs only the parallel idiomatic field.

translationRepairs.before: Han verdict digests yielded three hundred further fascicles after Decree A, while Minister Bao cataloged marriage suits into the Comparative Index—960 scrolls total.
translationRepairs.after: Han-era case decisions were collected as Ordinance A and following in more than three hundred chapters, while Minister over the Masses Lord Bao compiled decisions on marriage and litigation as the Legal Comparisons Catalogue, 906 scrolls in all.
translationRepairs.reason: 九百六卷 is 906, not 960, and 司徒鮑公 supplies Lord Bao's office. The existing proposal repairs only the idiomatic field.

translationRepairs.before: At Guanqiu Jian’s execution his son Dian’s wife Lady Xun faced collateral death; her clansman Yan, tied by marriage to Emperor Jing, memorialized the Wei emperor begging mercy.
translationRepairs.after: At Guanqiu Jian’s execution, his son Dian’s wife Lady Xun faced collateral death; her elder kinsman Xun Yi, connected by marriage to Sima Shi, memorialized the Wei emperor to beg for her life.
translationRepairs.reason: 顗 is Xun Yi, not Yan, and 景帝 here is Sima Shi. The existing proposal repairs only the idiomatic field.

translationRepairs.before: Specialists guarding text resemble Zhang Shi holding fast to the equal verdict on breaking the imperial avenue cordon.
translationRepairs.after: Specialists guarding the text resemble Zhang Shizhi holding fast to the impartial verdict on breaking the imperial procession cordon.
translationRepairs.reason: 釋之 is Zhang Shizhi; “Zhang Shi” truncates his name. The existing proposal repairs only the idiomatic field.

translationRepairs.before: As for extraordinary judgments or rewards exceeding statute—like Han founder killing Chu ministers for private motives or enfeoffing Lady Zhao without merit—only the lord monopolizes such acts; duty clerks may not emulate.
translationRepairs.after: As for extraordinary judgments and rewards or punishments outside the law—like the Han founder executing a Chu minister for his own reasons or enfeoffing a Zhao who had no merit—these belong to the ruler alone and are not for serving officials to propose.
translationRepairs.reason: 趙氏 does not support identifying the recipient as “Lady Zhao”; the existing proposal repairs the idiomatic omission but leaves this invented gender in the literal field.

translationRepairs.before: At that time Xiao He and Cao Shen had died—subordinates like Zhou Bo could not straighten principle.
translationRepairs.after: At that time Xiao He and Cao Shen had already died, and men like Zhou Bo and Guan Ying could not set the principle right.
translationRepairs.reason: 絳灌 names both Zhou Bo, Marquis of Jiang, and Guan Ying. The current literal field omits Guan Ying; the existing proposal repairs only the idiomatic field.

translationRepairs.before: As for marketplace execution clauses truly not unforgivable crimes hands not killers yet statutes lump equal severity blocking mitigation paths—Zhong Chen remonstrated hence Yuan emperor pitied.
translationRepairs.after: As for the marketplace-execution articles, these are not truly unpardonable crimes; even when no one was killed by the offender’s own hand, the code assigns the same penalty and blocks reduction. Zhong Yao and Chen Qun protested this, and Emperor Yuan paused over it in pity.
translationRepairs.reason: 鐘陳 refers to Zhong Yao and Chen Qun, not one person named “Zhong Chen.” The existing proposal repairs only the idiomatic field.

translationRepairs.before: Emperor Wu decided Han-Wei precedent was too muddled to govern by and ordered the chariot general, acting Secretariat chief, and Duke of Lu to recruit jurists and engrave a definitive code—that story follows.
translationRepairs.after: Emperor Wu decided earlier statutes were too uncertain to govern by and ordered the General of Chariots and Cavalry—acting Director of the Secretariat and Duke of Lu—to recruit talented men, revise the statutes, and establish their chapters.
translationRepairs.reason: 車騎將軍、守尚書令、魯公 are three titles of the one official being commissioned; the current coordination reads as an order to three people.

translationRepairs.before: Corvée delays, supply bungles, and edict disputes had been jammed into mismatched chapters; Wei isolated detention crimes once accidental overlap with capital military guilt was unwound.
translationRepairs.after: Corvée delays, supply failures, and failures to carry out edicts had been scattered across mismatched chapters; because Emperor Wen of Han’s Dingyou edict was no longer fit to serve as standing law, Wei separated these cases into the Detention Statute.
translationRepairs.reason: 《丁酉詔書》，漢文所下 explicitly attributes the edict to Emperor Wen of Han; the current idiomatic field omits both the named ruler and the edict.

translationRepairs.before: Under Sima Shi co-rule, daughters married out still died for parental treason.
translationRepairs.after: When Sima Shi served as regent, Wei law still executed daughters who had married out for a parent’s great treason.
translationRepairs.reason: 景帝輔政 says Sima Shi assisted the government as regent; “co-rule” incorrectly makes him a co-sovereign.

translationRepairs.before: the third year of Taishi (267 CE) saw the finished code presented to the throne.
translationRepairs.after: In the third year of Taishi, the completed code was presented to the throne.
translationRepairs.reason: The Chinese supplies only 泰始三年. The parenthetical Western year is not asserted by the current source and should not be introduced without separately reviewed calendar evidence.

translationRepairs.before: Punch Names threads severity of offenses, corrects scales of increase and decrease, releases manifold meanings across chapters, repairs insufficient clauses, and aligns overarching frameworks.
translationRepairs.after: Punishment Names sets out the relative severity of offenses, corrects the gradations of increase and reduction, clarifies the many meanings of the other chapters, supplements insufficient articles, and aligns their overarching principles.
translationRepairs.reason: 《刑名》 is Punishment Names; “Punch Names” is a definite title corruption.

translationRepairs.before: Recaptured rebels lose hair repeatedly—sentence spawning sentence;
translationRepairs.after: Convicts guilty of serious offenses who escape and let their hair grow past three inches are shaved again—punishment spawning punishment;
translationRepairs.reason: 重犯亡者 are serious offenders who escape, not rebels, and 發過三寸 is a specific condition omitted by the current field.

translationRepairs.before: castration follows rapists likewise.
translationRepairs.after: those guilty of illicit sex are castrated on the same reasoning.
translationRepairs.reason: 淫者 denotes offenders guilty of illicit sexual conduct; the source does not narrow the category to rape.

translationRepairs.before: Now take lighter capital cases and thrice-escaped lewd bandits—replace all with corporal sentences.
translationRepairs.after: Now the lighter cases within the range of capital punishment, together with those who have committed escape, illicit sex, or theft three times, should all have corporal punishment substituted for death.
translationRepairs.reason: 三犯逃亡淫盜 describes three-time offenders in the categories of escape, illicit sex, or theft; “thrice-escaped lewd bandits” fuses those categories into one description.

translationRepairs.before: Demote borderline capitals and chronic sex-thieves to mutilation.
translationRepairs.after: Substitute corporal punishment for the lighter capital cases and for offenders convicted three times of escape, illicit sex, or theft.
translationRepairs.reason: The current field collapses the separate offenses 逃亡、淫、盜 into “sex-thieves” and omits the three-offense threshold.

translationRepairs.before: Adult repeat offenders receive no quarter.
translationRepairs.after: Anyone outside these exempt groups who commits a crime must be punished without pardon; this is the principle of government.
translationRepairs.reason: 自非此族 refers to everyone outside the previously named old, young, and infirm groups; neither adulthood nor repeat offending appears in the source.

translationRepairs.before: Legal officers of fifth rank and above may lodge dissenting readings.
translationRepairs.after: Legal officers and their superiors may submit differing opinions when their interpretations diverge.
translationRepairs.reason: 法吏以上 does not specify the fifth rank; that rank is invented in the current field.

translationRepairs.before: Non-capital crimes received death.
translationRepairs.after: Thieves, illicit-sex offenders, and fugitives have killed no one and should therefore receive corporal rather than capital punishment.
translationRepairs.reason: 則加之以刑 advocates applying corporal punishment to the listed non-homicide offenders; the current field reverses the argument by saying they received death.

translationRepairs.before: Yuanxing era Huan Xuan reopened corporal debate.
translationRepairs.after: At the end of Emperor An’s Yuanxing era, regent Huan Xuan again proposed restoring amputation of either foot as a substitute for death and ordered the hundred officials to debate it.
translationRepairs.reason: The current field omits Huan Xuan’s regency, the specific proposal to amputate either foot, its purpose of reducing death sentences, and his order for an official-wide debate.

extractionIssues.issue: The person record's polity list is ["Western Jin", "Eastern Jin"], although Chen Chong is introduced under Emperor Zhang of Han, serves in Yongyuan 6, and the record itself describes him as an Eastern Han official.
extractionIssues.proposedResolution: Replace the polity list with ["Eastern Han"].
extractionIssues.reason: The current polity assignment contradicts the chapter context and the record’s own description.

chronologyNotes.note: The source gives the native date 泰始三年 only. The current idiomatic field's “267 CE” is an unsourced conversion in this chapter text and is removed by sr-013; no replacement Western year is proposed.

topFindings: The s0096 proposed repair still leaves authorship of the Spring and Autumn Adjudications grammatically attached to Zhang Tang; the replacement explicitly attributes it to Dong Zhongshu.
Eight existing idiomatic proposals leave the same name, number, or attribution defect in the literal field.
s0246 inserts an unsupported Western year, while s0211 miscasts Sima Shi’s regency as co-rule and s0525 reverses the corporal-punishment argument.
Chen Chong’s extraction record assigns him to Western and Eastern Jin despite the chapter and its own description placing him in Eastern Han.
